question.text: Which of the following correctly lists four key financial regulators in India?

explanation.text: The Logic: India's principal financial-sector statutory regulators are SEBI (securities markets and mutual funds), RBI (banking and monetary policy), IRDAI (insurance) and PFRDA (pension funds, including NPS). Each oversees a distinct segment of the financial system and is empowered to make and enforce regulations and adjudicate grievances within its domain. The Trap: Option B mixes SEBI with AMFI (an industry association) and CAMS / KFintech (Registrar and Transfer Agents — service providers, not regulators). Option C lists exchanges and a depository (NSE, BSE, NSDL) alongside RBI. Option D includes NISM, which is an investor-education and certification body rather than a regulator. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages reviewed mention SEBI, AMFI, RBI and aspects of insurance/NPS only incidentally and do not contain an explicit list naming SEBI, RBI, IRDAI and PFRDA together as the four key regulators. The framing above reflects publicly known Indian regulatory architecture rather than a direct workbook citation.
